subject: FintechCo API authn & key management - post-demo recap & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@fintechco.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: FintechCo API authn & key management - post-demo recap & next steps

Hi Alex -

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap while it's fresh and a proposed set of next steps so we can move the integration forward. Great to meet you and the FintechCo team - excited about the use case for embeddings + reranker on transaction data.

Recap (integration/architecture items we discussed):
- SDK setup: you plan to use the Redwood Node SDK in the backend service that handles customer requests. We'll provide a sample integration repo and quickstart.
- Authn options: recommended approach is service-accounts for server-to-server auth with short-lived JWTs (we sign/issue tokens via a managed token service) or OAuth2 for user-level consent flows.
- API keys: supported for low-privilege access (e.g., embeddings-only keys). Keys can be scoped by route/model and by tenant/project.
- Key rotation: supported via our rotation API and recommended 30-90 day rotation with automated rotation hooks into your KMS.
- KMS: we support customer-managed keys (bring-your-own-KMS) for secrets at rest; you can also use Redwood-managed keys.
- Routing & multitenancy: per-tenant routing (route-by-API-key or tenant-id) to enforce quota and model access policies.
- Structured output / tool-calling: we support tool-calling and JSON-schema enforcement; recommend a separate service account with restricted scopes for tool execution.
- Embeddings & reranker access control: separate keys for embeddings-only vs generation; allow limiter rules for vector search to avoid exfiltration.

Action items / next steps (proposed):
1) I'll send the sample service-account policy and a short key-rotation playbook (attached).
2) Can you confirm whether FintechCo will require BYOK (customer KMS) for token-signing and secrets? Reply with "BYOK: yes/no" and which provider (AWS KMS / GCP KMS / Azure Key Vault).
3) Dev to share the current auth flow (does your backend already mint short-lived JWTs?) and whether you have a per-tenant service-account pattern today.
4) Schedule a 30-min follow-up next week to walk through the sample integration and rotation webhooks; propose Tue 2026-06-29 10:00 PT or Wed 2026-06-30 09:00 PT.

Attachments: key_rotation_playbook.pdf (high-level runbook), sample_service_account_policy.json (example IAM policy)

Best,

Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com | (415) 555-0142
Redwood Inference
From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@fintechco.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2026 17:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FintechCo API authn & key management - post-demo recap & next steps

Thanks Marissa - really helpful recap. A couple quick clarifications from our side: we have two constraints to validate before the follow-up call: 

- BYOK: we require customer-managed KMS for production secrets (AWS KMS). Can Redwood integrate with our AWS KMS or will we need a gateway that rotates secrets into Redwood?

- Rotation automation: does Redwood provide a rotation webhook or API that we can call to trigger key swaps, or do you expect us to rotate keys purely on the client side? Ideally we want rotation to be auditable and triggerable from our CI/CD pipeline.

Also, on service accounts: we prefer a pattern where each environment (staging/prod) has a distinct service account with an auditable identity; can your sample policy show per-environment roles/least privilege?

Finally, one security ask from our infosec: can embeddings access be restricted so that embedding-only keys cannot call generation endpoints?

If you can answer those points ahead of the call it will speed validation on our side. Tuesday 6/29 10:00 PT works for me.

Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2026 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FintechCo API authn & key management - post-demo recap & next steps

Alex - thanks, answers inline below and attaching the policy/playbook for your infra team to review.

- BYOK: Yes, Redwood supports BYOK. For AWS KMS we can integrate via an external key provider flow: you can grant a service principal in your account permission to wrap/unwrap secrets, or you can push encrypted key material via our secure ingestion API. We'll include both options in the playbook.

- Rotation automation: we provide a Rotation API + webhook. Two common patterns:
  1) Redwood-managed rotation: Redwood calls your KMS to rotate secrets on your schedule and emits audit events to your SIEM (we support EventBridge / PubSub).
  2) Customer-triggered rotation: you call our rotation endpoint from CI/CD and we return new key material; the entire operation is logged and versioned.

Both are supported - I'll highlight pros/cons in the attached playbook.

- Service accounts: attached sample_policy shows per-environment roles (redwood:service-account:staging vs redwood:service-account:prod) and least-privilege example.

- Embeddings-only keys: yes - you can mint keys that are restricted by capability (embeddings_read, rerank_read) and prevented from generation endpoints. We'll include sample policy snippets.

Proposed follow-up: Tue 2026-06-29 10:00 PT confirmed. I'll send a calendar invite with a short agenda (sample integration walkthrough + rotation webhooks).

Attachments: key_rotation_playbook.pdf, sample_service_account_policy.json

Thanks - looking forward to the call.

Best,
Marissa
